Comment: CloudLab c240g5 (scripts/cloudlab/profile.py: node0 the control node, node1 to node4 the hosts of n1 to n4): the 4-node capacity (C4) of Quake's index of Wikipedia c1024: a flat k-means of round(sqrt(N)) = 3,939 lists, one replica a vector (fusion_build --from-index the base index --clustering kmeans; the base's IDs, raw-vector locations, codebook and page file; results/kmeans-index-2026-11-26), its 64 GP partitions with each head weighing its list's postings, the nodes started on its 4-node warmup snapshot (experiment.wiki-c1024-kmeans-cloudlab-gpu-warmup-4.json). From 100 q/s: a query scans far more postings here than on the base index, so C4 may lie below the base's rates. The Quake runs (experiment.wiki-c1024-kmeans-cloudlab-gpu-quake.json) take Rate = 0.6 x C4, floored to tens. NProbe, with --max-nprobe the same (the GPU's candidate buffers), is the smallest that reaches the base index's recall at nprobe 64, N 200 (0.8891), from the lab server's recall table (results/kmeans-index-2026-11-26/summary.txt): 96 (recall 0.9108; nprobe 64 gives 0.8863), as the trial there (experiment.wiki-c1024-kmeans-quake-trial.json) chose it.
